surprises.description: The preview treated about $105 million of adjusted EBITDA as the number to beat and said $112 million or more would be a genuine upside print. CTOS reported $111 million, above the central estimate but short of that upside threshold.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Treat $105M as the number to beat and $112M+ as a genuine upside print.”

surprises.description: The preview said reaffirming FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance was the most likely outcome. Instead, CTOS raised the range for the third time this year, while leaving revenue guidance unchanged.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance for the third time this year to $447.5 million-$460 million” and “affirming revenue guidance of $2.1 billion-$2.2 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Three outcomes, in descending order of frequency: reaffirm, narrow to the upper half (bullish), or trim to the low end (bearish).”

surprises.description: The preview expected net rental fleet investment of $170–200 million and more than $50 million of levered free cash flow. CTOS instead raised investment to $210–230 million, leaving levered free cash flow only slightly positive; most of the incremental units’ earnings are expected in 2027 rather than 2026.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raised 2026 net rental fleet investment to $210 million-$230 million (about $35 million above prior midpoint)” and “2026 levered free cash flow is now expected to be only slightly positive versus a prior expectation of more than $50 million,” with “most earnings deferred to 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 net rental fleet investment of $170–200M” and “The FY commitment to >$50M levered FCF.”

surprises.description: Q3 average utilization exceeded the preview’s 80% watch level, and management reported further improvement in Q4, with utilization above 84% and OEC on rent above $1.5 billion. That is a stronger near-term rental trend than the preview’s Q3-focused watch level alone implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Rental fleet utilization averaged 81.5% in Q3 (up 220 bps year-over-year) and has since surpassed 84% in Q4,” while “OEC on rent” rose from a Q3 average of $1.39 billion to “currently over $1.5 billion.”

surprises.description: Q3 average OEC on rent came in at $1.39 billion, just below the preview’s watch level of more than $1.40 billion, despite the stronger subsequent Q4 level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “OEC on rent rising from a Q3 average of $1.39 billion to currently over $1.5 billion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Avg. OEC on rent … Q3'26 Watch Level: >$1.40B.”

surprises.description: On-rent yield was 39.4%, just below the preview’s 39.5% threshold and unchanged from the cited Q2 level, rather than showing the sequential improvement the preview was watching for.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “On-rent yield: ≥39.5%” and “If yield comes in flat-to-down sequentially, the ‘transmission mix is structurally higher-yielding’ argument … takes real damage.”

surprises.description: The preview expected Q3 order strength to convert into STEM deliveries and flagged delivery slippage as a risk, but the reported third-party revenue fell 5%. More than $20 million of sales were delayed by a chassis recall and hailstorm, alongside a strategic shift of production to the rental fleet; management expects the delayed sales to reverse in Q4.
surprises.fact_evidence: “STEM third-party revenue (excluding intersegment sales) fell 5%,” affected by “over $20 million of sales delayed by a chassis vendor recall and a Kansas City hailstorm, both expected to reverse in Q4.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The quarter hinges on whether STEM converts the early-Q3 order strength into Q3 deliveries rather than Q4.”

surprises.description: The Q3 STEM backlog of $342 million was broadly in line with the preview’s expectation of more than $340 million, but its subsequent growth to nearly $400 million and the mid-to-high-teens expected Q4 sales growth add stronger forward demand evidence than that Q3 threshold alone suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “STEM new sales backlog ended Q3 at $342 million (up 22% year-over-year) and has since grown to nearly $400 million, with Q4 third-party new sales expected to rise at a mid-to-high teens rate year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Anything below ~$340M contradicts guidance”; the preview also noted backlog had already grown to “>$340M in early Q3.”

surprises.description: The preview highlighted the supportive sector backdrop for rental demand. CTOS reported strong SCR growth and profitability, including 18% segment revenue growth and a 54.6% adjusted EBITDA margin, although the preview did not set specific SCR revenue or margin estimates.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SCR segment revenue grew 18% to $223 million with segment adjusted EBITDA margin of 54.6% (up ~220 bps), rental gross margin near 79%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “The end-market backdrop for CTOS's rental segment should be a tailwind.”
